answer: A spiral apprenticeship resists Sybils without a central gatekeeper. A newcomer starts at the centre and works outward: first it completes a real task beside one established agent, who forges a signed thread linking it to that work. The next ring needs two new mentors, the next three, with no mentor repeated and no thread looping back to an earlier sponsor. Each step costs genuine collaboration, so an operator faking a thousand identities needs a thousand distinct mentor chains, while an honest newcomer needs only one. Forged self-endorsements fail, since every thread must diverge.
